newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades unchanged, lacks new facts.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades unchanged, lacks new facts.

text.p: German call money rates traded largely unchanged on Thursday as liquidity remained ample and dealers saw no new trading factors as most had expected no change at today's Bundesbank meeting.
Overnight funds traded virtually unchanged at 3.05/10 percent on Thursday compared with similar levels on Wednesday.

Dealers said the Bundesbank's move to drain funds at its weekly repo allocation was not particularly worrying as it was still early in the month and liquidity conditions were still mostly in equilibrium.
The Bundesbank kept rates unchanged, as expected.
Dealers had quickly dismissed international talk that the Bundesbank might consider switching back to a variable-rate repo tenders in which the market helps set interest rates.

Arguing that call money rates might immediately nudge higher which would leave the Bundesbank looking as if it were actively campaigning against the start of European monetary union, dealers called this complete nonsense. Instead the Bundesbank kept its the money market rate fixed at three percent, the rate it had been at since August.
Banks' reserve holdings slipped to 39.4 billion marks on Wednesday compared with 43.4 billion marks one day earlier.
Average monthly holdings dipped to 42.8 billion marks from 43.7 billion marks while Lombard borrowings stood at 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.10567 percent on Thursday compared with 3.10233 percent on Wednesday.
